icans: explain what a variation is and give an example from a Florida animal.

words: A difference in a characteristic between individuals of the same species, like one mouse with paler fur than another.
When a variation makes one individual more likely to survive and have young than others of the same species.
A group of animals of the same kind living in the same area, like all the beach mice on one island.
One single living thing in a population, with its own small differences.
A feature of a living thing, like fur color, bill length, or claw size. It means the same as trait.
Something an animal does that helps it survive, like digging a burrow or keeping watch for hawks.

parts.title: Not Every Individual Is the Same
parts.html: In Lesson 30.01, you learned that adaptations help animals survive. Now look closely at a population of one kind of animal. No two individuals are exactly alike. One beach mouse is paler. One tortoise has wider front legs. These small differences are called variations.

parts.title: When a Small Difference Matters
parts.html:
Most variations don't change much. But some do. In Florida scrub, fires sweep through every few years. A tortoise that digs a deeper burrow stays cooler underground, so its variation is a survival advantage.

Survivors have young, and the young can inherit the helpful characteristic. Scientists think this is how, over many generations, a whole population changes.

parts.title: Evidence and Animal Groups
parts.html: Scientists use evidence: observations and measurements, like a mouse's fur color or how deep a burrow goes. They also sort animals into groups. Mammals have fur, and most give birth to live young. Birds have feathers and lay eggs. Reptiles have dry scales. Amphibians have smooth, wet skin. Fish have gills. All of these are vertebrates, animals with a backbone. Insects have no backbone.

mix.q: Sam says, "Every difference between two animals is a survival advantage." What do you think?

options.t: Sam is right. Any difference helps an animal.
options.miss: Think about two tortoises with shells of slightly different brown. Would that help one survive a fire?

options.t: Most differences don't matter much. A difference is an advantage only if it helps with a real challenge.
options.ok: Yes! A deeper burrow helps in a fire, and pale fur helps on white sand. A slightly different shell color probably doesn't change much.

wow.title: Burrow City
wow.alt: A black racer snake lying at the mouth of a gopher tortoise burrow
wow.caption: A black racer snake at the door of a gopher tortoise burrow
wow.html:
A gopher tortoise burrow can be as long as a school bus. Deep inside, it stays cool in summer and safe during fires.

Scientists have found more than 350 kinds of animals using these burrows: snakes, frogs, mice, insects, and more.
wow.insetCap: A fresh burrow mouth in white sand.

keyIdea: Individuals in a population are not all the same. These small differences are called variations. Most variations don't matter much, but some give an individual a survival advantage, like a deeper burrow during a fire or pale fur on white sand. Survivors have young, and the young can inherit the helpful characteristic. Scientists use evidence, like observations and measurements, to find out which variations matter.

options.t: A body feature that every animal of a species shares in exactly the same form
options.miss: A variation isn't about being the same. It's a difference between individuals of the same species. Think about the pale mouse and the darker mouse.

options.t: A difference in a characteristic between individuals of the same species
options.ok: 🌿 Exactly right. A variation is a difference between individuals of the same kind, like a pale beach mouse and a darker mouse of the same species.

options.t: A brand-new trait that appears when two different species breed together
options.miss: A variation isn't about different species. It's a difference between individuals of the same species. Think about the pale mouse and the darker mouse.

quiz.q: A dry spell hits south Florida and the water drops. Spoonbill A has a slightly longer bill than Spoonbill B. What is the most likely outcome?

options.t: Spoonbill A struggles more because its longer bill is harder to sweep through shallow water
options.miss: Think about what changes during a dry spell: the food moves to deeper water. Which bill can still reach it?

options.t: Both spoonbills are equally affected because bill length doesn't change how deep they can reach
options.miss: Think about what changes during a dry spell: the food moves to deeper water. Which bill can still reach it?

options.t: Spoonbill A can still reach food in slightly deeper water, giving it a survival advantage during the dry spell
options.ok: 🌿 Right! The dry spell is what makes the variation matter. Spoonbill A's longer bill gives it an advantage because the water level dropped.

quiz.q: Which statement best describes how a variation becomes a survival advantage?

options.t: A variation becomes an advantage when it helps one individual survive a specific challenge in its environment better than others of the same kind
options.ok: ⭐ Exactly! The environment and the challenge are what make the variation matter. Most variations don't help or hurt, but some, in the right situation, make a real difference.

options.t: Every difference between animals is a survival advantage because any variation is better than none
options.miss: Think about the tortoises. A deeper burrow only mattered because of what happened: the fire. That's what turns a small difference into a survival advantage.

options.t: A variation only becomes an advantage if it creates a completely new species over time
options.miss: Think about the tortoises. A deeper burrow only mattered because of what happened: the fire. That's what turns a small difference into a survival advantage.
